how many laws of thermodynamics are ther: There are four laws of thermodynamics, numbered zeroth through third. The zeroth defines temperature, the first conserves energy, the second says entropy increases, and the third says absolute zero is unreachable.
which element has the highest melting po: Carbon has the highest melting/sublimation point of any element, about 3,600 °C (at normal pressure graphite sublimes rather than melts). Tungsten has the highest melting point of any metal, at 3,422 °C.
what is the hottest planet in the solar: Venus is the hottest planet, at about 465 °C (870 °F), thanks to a thick carbon dioxide atmosphere that creates a runaway greenhouse effect. Mercury is closer to the Sun but cools at night.
what is the powerhouse of the cell?: Mitochondria generate most of a cell's ATP, the molecule that stores energy. They have their own DNA, passed down from the mother.
what is the first element on the periodi: Hydrogen, atomic number 1, is the lightest and most abundant element in the universe. The periodic table is ordered by atomic number.
how many chromosomes are in your body ce: Human body cells (somatic cells) have 46 chromosomes, or 23 pairs. Egg and sperm cells have 23 chromosomes.
about what percentage of the earth's sur: About 71% of Earth's surface is covered by water, and most of it is in the oceans. That's why the planet looks blue from space.
how many planets make up our solar syste: The Solar System has eight planets, since Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006. They are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.
99.95% of an atom's mass is in which par: Almost all of an atom's mass is in the nucleus, made of protons and neutrons. Electrons are about 1,800 times lighter.
which scientist gave his name to the uni: The ampere, the unit of electric current, is named after the French physicist André-Marie Ampère. He founded electrodynamics in the 1820s.

how far along are you approximately, whe: Most women feel the baby's first movements ("quickening") between 16 and 25 weeks, often around 18-20. First-time mothers feel it later.
the surface of this planet is unique, it: Earth is the only known planet with large amounts of liquid water on its surface. Other worlds may have subsurface oceans, such as Europa.

pre-eclampsia, thought to be caused by i: Pre-eclampsia is a pregnancy complication of high blood pressure and organ stress, usually after 20 weeks. It needs medical monitoring.

this is one of the most common health pr: Being overweight raises the risk of high blood pressure (hypertension), as well as diabetes and heart disease. Weight loss can help lower blood pressure.
in the usa, obesity is the second leadin: In the US, obesity has been described as the second leading cause of preventable death, after smoking. Both affect heart disease and cancer risk.
which of the following has the most fat?: Blue cheese is high in fat, with about 30% of its weight as fat. Compare labels, since fat varies among cheeses.

laughter is one of the first expressions: Babies start laughing at around three to four months of age. It's one of the first social expressions.
which part of the body is decomposed las: Hair and nails are some of the slowest parts of a body to decompose, since they're made of tough keratin. Bones last longer.
due to this, there is almost no atmosphe: The Moon's gravity is about one-sixth of Earth's, too weak to hold a substantial atmosphere. Any gases escape into space.
when was the moon formed?: The Moon formed about 4.5 billion years ago, probably when a Mars-sized body (Theia) hit the early Earth. The debris combined into the Moon.
moons shape is not quite round. what doe: The Moon is slightly egg-shaped, not a perfect sphere, because of Earth's tidal forces. Its surface is also covered with craters.

if you were taking a course in entomolog: Entomology is the study of insects. The Greek "entomon" means insect.
people with this disorder have difficult: Autism spectrum disorder affects communication and social interaction, in varying degrees. It is a spectrum.

during this month of the pregnancy women: Hormonal changes in early pregnancy can cause mood swings. They often peak in the first trimester.

what does www stand for?: WWW stands for World Wide Web, a system of linked pages invented by Tim Berners-Lee in 1989. It isn't the same as the internet.
".com" stands for "commercial". It was one of the original top-level domains.
what is the speed of light in free space: Light travels at about 299,792 km/s (186,282 miles per second) in a vacuum. Nothing with mass can reach this speed.
what is the main purpose of pulleys?: Pulleys change the direction of a force and, in combinations, reduce the effort needed to lift a load. The trade-off is that you pull more rope.
which planet was named after the roman g: Mars is named after the Roman god of war, because of its red color, like blood. Its moons, Phobos and Deimos, mean fear and dread.

which of the following doctors is least: Emergency physicians work in shifts, so they are not typically "on call" at home. Many other specialists take call.
what do we call the ratio of a circles c: Pi (π) is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter, approximately 3.14159. It's an irrational number.
what do we call the base for natural log: The number e (≈ 2.71828) is the base of natural logarithms. It's named after Leonhard Euler.
botox (botulinum toxin) is used to treat: Botox is approved to treat chronic migraine, as well as muscle spasms, excessive sweating and more. It was originally studied for eye muscle disorders.
how long on average does it take for the: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth. The Sun is about 150 million km away.
how much does human hair grow in a year?: Human hair grows about 1.25 cm (half an inch) per month, or around 15 cm (6 inches) a year. Growth varies from person to person.

what does ludology study?: Ludology is the study of games, especially video games. It comes from the Latin "ludus", game.

what day is internationally recognised a: World AIDS Day is on December 1 each year. It was first held in 1988.

what is the symbol for vanadium?: Vanadium's symbol is V. It's named after Vanadis, a Norse goddess.
what is the symbol for polonium?: Polonium's symbol is Po. Marie Curie discovered it and named it after her native Poland.
what is the symbol for magnesium?: Magnesium's symbol is Mg. It's the lightest structural metal.

what is the symbol for cobalt?: Cobalt's symbol is Co. It gives a deep blue color to glass.
what is the symbol for iron?: Iron's symbol is Fe, from the Latin "ferrum". It's the most common element on Earth by mass.
what is the symbol for thallium?: Thallium's symbol is Tl. It's a toxic metal that was once used as rat poison.
grasslands cover this part of land on ea: Grasslands cover about a fifth of the Earth's land (some estimates are higher, up to 40% including savannas). They include prairies, steppes and pampas.
deserts are advancing and taking over th: Deserts are expanding in the Sahel and other regions due to drought, overgrazing and climate change. The rate varies by place.
in the winter of 1998-1999 this u.s. sta: Washington State's Mount Baker Ski Area received 1,140 inches (95 ft) of snow in 1998-99, a record. It beat Mount Rainier's 1971-72 record.

which of these is classified on the hami: The Hamilton-Norwood scale classifies stages of male pattern baldness. It was developed in the 1950s-70s.
anemometers, from the greek word anemos: An anemometer measures wind speed (and some types, pressure). The word comes from the Greek "anemos" for wind.
how long can a total lunar eclipse last?: A total lunar eclipse can last up to around 1 hour 47 minutes in totality. The whole process takes hours.
the implementation of mpas is one way to: MPA stands for Marine Protected Area, a section of ocean with restrictions on fishing or other activities. They help coral reefs and marine life recover.
this country is the worlds largest expor: Indonesia is the world's largest exporter of corals, for the aquarium and decor trade. Collection can damage reefs.
what is the most common reason for getti: Relaxation is the most common reason people get a massage. Others are pain relief and injury recovery.
smooth strokes are enhanced by this subs: Massage oils reduce friction so the therapist can use smooth strokes. Common oils include almond and jojoba.
as massage relaxes the body, relieves pa: Massage is linked to reduced stress and muscle tension, which can improve sleep. Studies have shown some benefit.
what is the predominant mood of a person: Anxiety is mainly characterized by fear and worry. It's a common condition that can be treated.

in geometry, which angles are called opp: Opposite (vertical) angles are formed by two intersecting lines and are equal. They are across from each other.

what is the symbol for boron?: Boron's symbol is B, atomic number 5. Borax contains boron.
what is the symbol for neon?: Neon's symbol is Ne, atomic number 10. It glows reddish-orange in signs.
what is the symbol for sulfur?: Sulfur's symbol is S, atomic number 16. It's yellow and smells when burned.
what is the symbol for bismuth?: Bismuth's symbol is Bi, atomic number 83. Pepto-Bismol contains a bismuth compound.
what is the symbol for platinum?: Platinum's symbol is Pt, atomic number 78. It's a rare, dense metal used in jewelry and catalytic converters.
what is the symbol for cadmium?: Cadmium's symbol is Cd, atomic number 48. It is toxic and used in batteries.

which of effect of these is the main rea: The Sun's energy drives the water cycle, evaporating water from oceans and land. Gravity brings it back as precipitation.

evapotranspiration is a term connected t: Evapotranspiration is the movement of water from soil and plants into the air. It combines evaporation and transpiration from plants.

osteology is an important part of physic: An osteologist studies bones. Osteology is key in anthropology and forensic science.

if you studied petrology, where would yo: Petrology is the study of rocks, their origin and composition. The Greek "petra" means rock.

deoxyribonucleic acid (dna), the molecul: DNA is replicated during the S (synthesis) phase of the cell cycle, between G1 and G2. This ensures each daughter cell gets a full copy.

according to the electromagnetic spectru: Gamma rays are the most energetic part of the electromagnetic spectrum, with the shortest wavelengths. They come from nuclear processes and cosmic events.
what computational device was designed b: Charles Babbage designed the Difference Engine in the 1820s, a mechanical calculator, and later the Analytical Engine. The latter is considered a forerunner of computers.
which of these is represented by the che: C12H22O11 is the formula for sucrose (table sugar). Lactose and maltose have the same formula.
what is the maximum angle of field of vi: Compound eyes can have a very wide field of view, up to nearly 360° in some insects, such as dragonflies. They detect motion well.
there is a unit called a yottagram. how: A yottagram is 10^24 grams. Yotta is the largest SI prefix, together with ronna and quetta.
which nation issued the first metric cur: The US introduced a decimal currency with the Coinage Act of 1792 (a dollar of 100 cents). Russia had a decimal ruble earlier, under Peter the Great.

a ionic compound with h (hydrogen) in th: Compounds that start with H, such as HCl, are usually acids because they release hydrogen ions in water. Water itself is an exception.
what is soap?: Soap is made from fats and a strong base, and is slightly basic. It feels slippery and tastes bitter.

approximately how long is one astronomic: One astronomical unit is the average distance from Earth to the Sun, about 149.6 million km (93 million miles). It is used for distances in the Solar System.

the usa leads� the world in per capita c: The US has among the highest water use per person in the world, with Canada close behind. Much of it goes to irrigation and household use.

one of the most basic characteristics of: Forgetting is considered adaptive, since it clears out unneeded information. It helps the brain focus on what matters.

this disorder, also known as manic depre: Bipolar disorder involves episodes of mania and depression, and has an elevated suicide risk. Treatment helps; in the US you can call or text 988 for crisis support.

a twin fetus which does not develop duri: A vanishing twin is a fetus in a multiple pregnancy that dies in the womb and is reabsorbed. It happens in many pregnancies.
